html:
The Miami, or Myaamia, are an Algonquian people of what is now Indiana and western Ohio. They speak Miami-Illinois, the language also spoken by the Illinois Confederation.

In the 1600s, during the Beaver Wars, they took refuge in Wisconsin, then returned to the Wabash and Maumee rivers. Their main town, Kekionga, stood where Fort Wayne is now. They traded with New France and then the British.

After American independence, the Miami chief Little Turtle led a Native alliance with the Shawnee and others in the Northwest Indian War. They crushed a US army under Arthur St. Clair in 1791, then lost at Fallen Timbers in 1794, and signed the Treaty of Greenville in 1795, giving up most of Ohio. More land went in later treaties. In 1846 most Miami were removed to Kansas and later Oklahoma, while some families stayed in Indiana.
